title: Technical SEO for Solar Websites: What to Review
html:
Start with discovery and indexing

A technical review checks whether search engines can access important solar service pages. Review HTTP status codes, robots directives, canonical URLs, internal links and the XML sitemap. Use Search Console to distinguish pages excluded intentionally from pages that should be available in search. A crawlable page is eligible for discovery; it is not guaranteed to be indexed or rank.

Organize services around customer needs

Give residential installation, commercial projects and other genuinely distinct services clear destinations. Connect those pages with useful navigation and relevant project examples. Avoid creating near-identical pages for every town. The structure should help a homeowner understand the offer and help search engines discover the content.

Measure performance before choosing fixes

Use real-user Core Web Vitals data where available, supported by laboratory tests. Review loading, responsiveness and visual stability on mobile. Large images, unnecessary scripts and shifting layouts are common areas to investigate. Performance improvements can help visitors use the site, but passing Core Web Vitals does not guarantee high rankings. Relevance, helpful content and other signals also matter.

Plan URL changes carefully

Map changed URLs to relevant replacements, use permanent redirects for moved content and update internal links. Keep valuable existing pages when their purpose remains useful. Monitor errors and indexing after a migration. Redirects reduce avoidable disruption; they cannot guarantee that all visibility will remain unchanged.

Keep local business information accurate

Publish the actual services and coverage of the solar business. Where the business is eligible for a Google Business Profile, ensure its details reflect real operations. Structured data should match visible content. Neither schema nor a technical adjustment guarantees a Google Maps position.

Agree on the work and the evidence

Separate audit findings from implementation. Your proposal should identify affected pages, priorities, responsibilities, development hours and validation. Review resolved crawl errors, important-page indexing, real-user performance and qualified inquiries where tracking supports them. Timing depends on the issue, the website and search-engine processing; do not treat a fixed number of weeks as a promised ranking outcome.

What does solar technical SEO cost?

Cost depends on the website, the issues found and the implementation effort. Ask for an itemized audit and repair scope, including what is excluded. Compare deliverables and responsibility for implementation before comparing prices.

How does this connect with wider SEO?

Technical SEO supports useful service content and an understandable customer journey. It works alongside accurate business information, original project evidence and ongoing review. Explore our SEO service for the commercial scope, or discuss a specific website issue with the team.

Sources: Google: Page experience; Google: Crawling.
